title: Supremacy
subtitle: AI, ChatGPT, and the Race That Will Change the World
pitch: The story of Demis Hassabis and Sam Altman, two idealists who set out to build safe AGI and ended up tied to big tech.

chapters.g: Opens with the race between two founders and two labs.
Demis Hassabis, chess and games prodigy.
Early worries about AI risk among the founders.
Hassabis's neuroscience and the founding of DeepMind.
Funding AGI dreams with investor money.
DeepMind's AlphaGo and the power of game playing AI.
Inside Google after the DeepMind deal.
Independent labs need giant companies to survive.
Scaling up models, and the costs.
OpenAI and Microsoft, DeepMind and Google.
Researchers who questioned the hype and raised present harms.
The launch and the race it started.
What concentrated power in AI means for everyone.

ideas: Both DeepMind and OpenAI began with safety minded ideals.
Both ended up bound to big tech money.
Competition and monopoly shape AI more than ideals.

args.a: The AGI race has been captured by a few giant companies.
args.c: Some argue big company resources also fund more safety research than small labs could.

questions: Could Hassabis or Altman have stayed independent?
Is concentration of AI power a safety risk or a safety help?

quiz.q: Which two founders does Supremacy follow?
quiz.w: Demis Hassabis of DeepMind and Sam Altman of OpenAI.
Independent labs ended up needing big tech to fund them.
